pathfinders-of-the-west-being-the-thrill:
Agnes C. Laut's Pathfinders of the West, copyrighted in 1904, tells the adventures of the men who opened the Great Northwest. The title names three of them: Radisson, La Vérendrye, and Lewis and Clark. Illustrations by Frederic Remington and others accompany the text.

In a letter at the front, Laut explains that while living in the Far West she tried to trace the explorers' paths herself. All the authorities led back to one main source of information. Her book turns that research into a lively narrative of fur traders, voyageurs, and the first crossings of a continent.
